newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish slightly higher.

text.p: Defying Wall Street's downturn, French shares finished slightly higher on Monday in a session dominated by technical trade on the last day of the monthly settlement.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 5.10 points or 0.18 percent higher while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 13 points at 2,758.0.
Volume totalled 9.1 billion francs. The level was swollen by numerous block trades.
The market started lower but then turned higher late in the day amid position-squaring.
Dealers said the market was sluggish and predicted that it would remain quiet for the next couple of days in the absence of expected major market moving news.

The aviation and aeronautics sector got a lift from new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's speech to an international air show in Paris on Saturday in which he appeared signal more openness to restructuring in the field.
Dassault Aviation climbed 7.41 percent to 1,160 francs, Lagardere gained 4.41 percent to 170.50 and Thomson-CSF rose 1.59 percent to 153.0.
Food group Eridania gained 4.19 percent to 896 francs, helped by a favourable outlook for its beet crop thanks to recent rain.

Shares in tobacco company Seita finished 0.26 percent higher at 190.50 francs after share analysts judged the landmark accord between U.S. authorities and cigarette companies was unlikely to spur action against European tobacco groups.
"It's wrong to see a settlement in the States as an opportunity to pursue tobacco companies in other countries," one analyst said.

After the closure, French financial markets regulator CMF said U.S. fund Templeton Global Investors held 5.01 percent of the capital of Banque Nationale de Paris through investment fund and client accounts. It said this stake represented 5.03 percent of BNP voting rights. BNP finished 2.12 percent higher at 226.70 francs.
